data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"A decentralized network of small services is more resilient to correlated failure than a monolith with superior redundancy because it replaces homogeneous redundancy with operational heterogeneity, which breaks the causal chain of systemic triggers.","counterconditions":[{"case":"The decentralized network adopts a standardized 'best practice' stack (e.g., all using the same cloud provider's managed Kubernetes version), creating a virtual monolith.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"The monolith employs N-version programming or heterogeneous redundancy (different implementations of the same spec across its internal nodes).","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"The mechanism is 'Type Diversity'. In a monolith, redundancy is typically identical (same binary, same OS, same config), meaning a single trigger (e.g., a specific packet sequence) causes a 100% failure rate regardless of the number of nodes. In a decentralized network, the lack of a central authority leads to idiosyncratic implementation choices (different languages, OS versions, hardware), which prevents a single trigger from activating the failure mode across the majority of the network.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
